scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Trata is traditionally performed in Megara in Attica and across the Aegean Islands.
Popular local history in Megara ties the performance to the Ottoman era, alleging it commemorates the construction of the chapel of Saint John the Dancer in a single day.

However, folklorists argue that the dance's core movement—mimicking the pulling in of fishing nets—points to an origin much older than the Ottoman period, rooted in ancient rites intended to ensure successful fishing.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance symbolizes fishing and celebrates the daily success of fishermen.
In Megara, it takes place every two years on Bright Tuesday (the Tuesday after Easter) as a commemorative ritual.
In the Aegean Islands, it is performed at all social functions and gatherings.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance features physical movements that imitate the action of hauling in fishing nets.
In Megara, women perform the dance together on the open space outside the chapel of Saint John the Dancer.
In the Aegean Islands, the dance takes the form of a Syrtos, featuring specific movements performed during the chorus on islands such as Ikaria.
Watch for Net-hauling motion.
